one_liner: Senior supervisor in ICE's budget office who manages relations with congressional appropriations committees and OMB, drafting testimony, briefings and appropriations responses.
fit_summary: Daniel's policy knowledge, relationship skills and government-client consulting at IEM are relevant, but this GS-15 requires one year of GS-14-equivalent specialized experience in appropriations work: preparing hearing and mark-up materials, drafting legislative language, and answering Appropriations Committee questions. Unless Daniel's IEM role involved senior-level appropriations or budget-legislation work, Daniel is unlikely to meet the minimum qualifications. There is no education substitute at this grade.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens) under Direct Hire Authority; ICTAP applies only to former federal employees, so it does not apply to Daniel.
One year of specialized experience at the GS-14 level or equivalent in appropriations and legislative analysis is required by the closing date; education cannot substitute.
A Top Secret clearance is required, and the selectee must pass a pre-employment drug test and random drug testing.
Applicants must pass the USA Hire online assessment cut score and complete the questionnaire.
This is an in-person job in Washington, DC, with no telework and no remote work.
strategy: Before applying, honestly compare Daniel's IEM work with each specialized-experience bullet; apply only if Daniel can point to a year of senior-level work on appropriations, federal budget requests, or legislative analysis.

If Daniel's IEM work touched FEMA or DHS disaster funding (for example, supplemental appropriations, Disaster Relief Fund analysis, or congressional inquiries), describe it specifically and concretely without copying the announcement wording.
Keep the resume to two pages, and list hours per week, exact dates, and supervisory or leadership scope for each role.

Answer the questionnaire truthfully at the level Daniel actually performed, since overstating can lead to removal. Prepare for the USA Hire assessment, which covers competencies such as decisiveness, resilience, and interpersonal skills.

Submit by November 4, 2026. As a more realistic route, target GS-11 to GS-13 congressional affairs, budget, or legislative analyst jobs at FEMA or DHS, or Hill staff roles, to build appropriations experience.
resume_bullets: Analyzed [legislation/appropriations bill] for budgetary impacts on [client agency] disaster recovery programs, producing [number] issue papers for [audience]. ([X] hrs/week, [dates])
Drafted [briefing packages/talking points/testimony support] for [client officials] ahead of [congressional hearings/OMB meetings], coordinating with [stakeholders].

interview_questions: Describe a time you prepared materials for an appropriations hearing or a committee mark-up. What was your role?
How would you build working relationships with Appropriations Committee staff and OMB examiners?
Tell us about a time you had to deliver an unwelcome budget message to a stakeholder.
How would you supervise a team responding to multiple urgent congressional requests at once?
